barriers.description: General practitioners (GPs) were not involved in the early context-of-use and user-requirements analysis nor the first usability pilot, limiting designers' access to a key stakeholder group.
barriers.justification: GP nonparticipation reduced the design team's ability to manage user understanding and facilitate user involvement for a multidisciplinary system, constraining requirement specification and early evaluation activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In this study, the GPs, one group of users, are not involved in the context of use and user requirements analysis and the first usability evaluation pilot.

barriers.description: Home care nurses did not perform the intended daily triage because of workload and unfamiliarity with the task, leading them to share triage responsibilities.
barriers.justification: Nurses' limited capacity and need to adapt prevented designers from observing and evaluating the intended workflow, hindering understanding of the real context of use and integration of feedback into design iterations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Home care nurses indicated that the daily triage of the report problems was necessary but not performed as intended because of workload and because they needed to get used to the daily task. Therefore, some home care nurses decided to share the triage task with nurses who had the capability to perform a triage.

barriers.description: The monitoring system lacked integration with electronic patient files, making adding new client profiles time-consuming and dependent on manual entry.
barriers.justification: Absence of EHR integration (an external technical/organizational constraint) limited designers' ability to evaluate real-world workflows and specify usable requirements for data entry and patient-management tasks.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Adding new client profiles in the monitoring and consulting webpage was experienced as time-consuming. ... Home care workers mentioned that a link between the electronic patient file and the monitoring and consulting webpage is desirable and will ensure that data of clients who are added to the home care will be automatically added to the monitoring and consulting webpage.

barriers.description: Feedback from GPs and pharmacists was relayed to home health care assistants by telephone rather than directly through the system, which was experienced as time-consuming.
barriers.justification: This communication workaround hindered designers' ability to evaluate and support integrated multidisciplinary feedback flows and constrained iterative improvements to in-system feedback mechanisms.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Home care nurses informed home health care assistants about the feedback of a GP or pharmacist by a telephone call, which was experienced as time consuming. The solution to forward feedback of a home care nurse, a GP, or a pharmacist from the monitoring and consulting webpage to the report webpage was mentioned.
